  Regular Meeting Minutes
  November 9, 2023

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Vice Chair Ruiz

ROLL CALL - by Ana Medina, Sr. Secretary
Present: Chair Alan Flores, Vice Chair Lizette Ruiz, Commissioners Edgar Pelayo and Adolfo Varas.
Secretary Jennifer Cypert had an excused absence.
Staff: Director Steve Costley, Deputy Director Tina Fierro, and Parks Superintendent Glenn Massey

APPROVAL OF MINUTES FOR: SEPTEMBER 14, 2023:
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve the minutes as presented
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Varas ; a roll call vote was taken, and motion was unanimously
approved

PUBLIC COMMENT
RECOGNIZED: Mario Dominguez, SG resident asked how dog feces were handled at the Parks. Director
Costley explained there are bag stations throughout South Gate & Hollydale Regional Parks.

PRESENTATION: ART IN PUBLIC PLACES APPLICATION UPDATE
Director Costley introduced representatives from TPL; showing the two new fonts for the mural.

OPEN SESSION ITEMS
1. ART IN PUBLIC PLACES APPLICATION UPDATE
Recommended Motion: Discuss the proposed lettering font and provide direction for staff or TPL to
either forward the Commission’s recommendation to the project manager or return to artist for changes.
M/S/C: Commissioner Varas/Commissioner Pelayo; a roll call vote was taken; motion unanimously
approved.
Director Costley reviewed this item and reminded the Commission the mural was approved at the last
meeting today is only to discuss the font; he then introduced the TPL representatives; a discussion ensued.
A motion was made to approve option #2 and forward on to City Council.
RECOGNIZED: Mario Dominguez, SG resident voiced his opinions on the designs, colors, and font for the
mural for the Art in Public Places Update and wanted the item brought back to change the mural.

2. RECREATION DIVISION – 1ST QUARTER REPORT FY 2023/24
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Varas; a roll call vote was taken; motion unanimously approved.
Deputy Dir. Fierro reviewed this item; a discussion ensued.
Commissioner Varas is excited to hear how good things are going. Vice Chair Ruiz congratulated staff on
the LA84 grant. Offered her help on getting the word out on events; Director Costley explained that a
Marketing Coordinator has been hired to help with social media. Chair Flores thanked staff for the
report.

  3. GROUNDS & FACILITY DIVISION 1st QUARTER REPORT FY 2023(24
 Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file
 M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Commissioner Varas; a roll call vote was taken; motion unanimously
 approved.
 Parks Supt. Massey reviewed this item, he explained that during this time of the year staff concentrates
 on routine maintenance. Vice Chair Ruiz noticed the tree trimming, good job. Chair Flores stated he
 appreciates how clean the park is especially after events. A discussion ensued.
 RECOGNIZED: Mario Dominguez, SG resident asked what kind of tree is in Triangle Park and would like to
 see a turkey giveaway. Parks Supt. Massey replied that he doesn’t remember the name of tree.

4. PARK SECURITY UPDATE
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file
M/S/C: Commissioner Varas/Vice Chair Ruiz; a roll call vote was taken; motion was unanimously
approved.
Parks Supt. Massey reviewed this item. Commissioner Pelayo has noticed changes in the Park and has
seen CSOs & Executive Management in the Park. Commissioner Varas stated that safety is his main
concern. Homelessness is a number one issue, thank you to staff for addressing these issues.
RECOGNIZED: Mario Dominguez, SG resident asked if the CSOs can give tickets, Director Costley
responded, yes.

 DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
 Director Costley: Thank you for judging the Halloween Costume contests; it took twelve minutes to get
 everyone in the gate. The Fencing Project preconstruction meeting was today; work will start December
 11. Different areas will be closed a a time. Goals and objectives will be brought to the Commission in
 December’s meeting. Meet the new City Manager, Ron Huston, on November 11 at 4pm at the Civic
 Center. Pageant of the Trees is December 2 at 4pm.

 Deputy Dir. Fierro: The Art Walk was October 14; Senator Rendon presented a check for 2.7 million that
 will go towards a couple of projects. On October 22 the Aquatics staff will host the first Pumpkin Plunge
 event. Family Day in the Park will be held November 4; Special Olympics will be the same day in a
 different area of the Park. November 11 at 11 am will be the Veteran’s Day Event. 5-on-5 Ball’n After
 Dark event will be November 22. On December 5 will be the Winter Wonderland Event and Tree Lighting
 along with the PD’s Feliz Navidad event. And lastly on December 9 is Breakfast with Santa.

 Parks Supt. Massey: Staff is working with Tree People of Los Angeles to plant trees in City parks. We
 have received the flail mower that will be used primarily in Hollydale Regional Park.

 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION SUB-COMMITTEE REPORTS
Commissioner Varas: Thank you to staff, had a wonderful time at the Halloween event, great job.

Vice Chair Ruiz: Judging the Halloween event was hard; enjoyed the Art Walk event.

Commissioner Pelayo: Was sorry he missed the Halloween event.

Chair Flores: Got there late but enjoyed it anyway. Sofive is doing changes, is it possible for them to do a
presentation; Director Costley replied he will ask them, but we don’t have any authority over them.

  Regular Meeting Minutes
  December 14, 2023

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Commissioner Varas

ROLL CALL - by Ana Medina, Sr. Secretary
Present: Chair Alan Flores and Commissioners Edgar Pelayo and Adolfo Varas. Chair Flores Vice Chair
Lizette Ruiz and Secretary Jennifer Cypert had excused absences.
Staff: Director Steve Costley, Deputy Director Tina Fierro, and Parks Superintendent Glenn Massey

PUBLIC COMMENTS - None

OPEN SESSION ITEMS

1. GROUNDS MAINTENANCE DIVISION ANNUAL REPORT
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Commissioner Varas/Commissioner Pelayo; a roll call vote was taken, and motion was unanimously
approved.
Parks Supt. Massey reviewed this item; Staff repaired the irrigation system and planted 300 Lantana plants
adjacent to the riverbank at Hollydale Regional Park. A total of seven trees were removed due to disease
and/or structural failure, over 40 trees were planted in their stead. Chair Flores asked how new trees are
protected; Parks Supt. Massey explained that staff tries to protect them but sometimes they do die or
broken, that’s why 40 trees were planted. A discussion ensued.

2. GOALS AND PERFORMANCE MEASURES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024/25
Recommended Motion: Approve the proposed Goals and Performance Measures for FY 2024/25.
M/S/C: Commissioner Varas/Commissioner Pelayo; a roll call vote was taken, and motion was unanimously
approved.
Director Costley explained this item; this is part of the yearly budget process presented to the
Commissioners to show what staff will be working on in the coming fiscal year. A discussion ensued.

3. ANNUAL REPORT ON IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PARKS & RECREATION MASTER PLAN
Recommended Motion: Approve the proposed Goals and Performance Measures for FY 2024/25.
M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/ Commissioner Varas; a roll call vote was taken, and motion was
unanimously approved.
Director Costley explained this item. Since this Master Plan is 15 years old and much of it has been
implemented Council would like staff to start the process for a new one this upcoming year. A discussion
ensued.

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Director Costley: Rotary hosted the annual Thanksgiving Luncheon on Thanksgiving day, Pageant of the
Trees was once again a big success as was Breakfast with Santa. The Winter Wonderland event was highly
successful with an estimated attendance of 3,000. The park will be closed for the holidays with the Golf
Course and Sports Center being open. Will be going on vacation for three weeks starting tomorrow.

  Page 1 of 2
  9
 Deputy Dir. Fierro: Veteran’s Day event was well attended and hats and medals were handed out to the
attending veterans. People really enjoyed the snow sledding at the Winter Wonderland event; Breakfast
with Santa was again a very good event with 400 in attendance. The Christmas Parade and Santa’s Village
toy give-away was enjoyed by all who attended. Surfing with Santa will be this Saturday the pool.

Parks Supt. Massey: Both Grounds and Facility Maintenance staff assisted at all the special events;
Grounds staff have worked on the diamonds, Diamond 1 is getting new sod. The tree trimming has been
completed at SG Park.

PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION SUB-COMMITTEE REPORTS
Chair Flores: Good job in getting the word out and having great turnout. Thank you to staff for how well
they clean up the park after the events. Happy Holidays to everyone.

Commissioner Pelayo: Wish everyone Happy Holidays

Commissioner Varas: All the Centennial events have been great, thanks to staff for their hard work.

REQUEST FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS - None

ADJOURNMENT - At 8:40 p.m. Chair Flores asked for a motion to adjourn.
M/S/C: Commissioner Varas/Commissioner Pelayo

Respectfully submitted:

Jennifer Cypert, Secretary
Parks & Recreation Commission

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 1
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Parks & Recreation Director
Date:  January 24, 2024

Subject:  Reorganization

Recommended Motion: The Commission must nominate and approve a Chair, Vice-
Chair, and Secretary for the coming year.

Report Summary: As has been the practice of the Commission, each May, at the
regular Commission meeting, nominations and elections are held to appoint a new
Chair, Vice-Chair and Secretary for the Commission for the coming year. This year in
keeping with the State Elections the reorganization has been moved to December.
Normally, these positions become effective immediately.

The Chair should solicit nominations from the members present, beginning with
nominations for Chair. Once all commissioners have had the opportunity to make a
nomination for each position, discussion should be allowed and a vote, confirming the
appointments slate is made.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Jose Covarrubias, Facility Maintenance Supervisor
Date:  March 27, 2024

Subject:  Park Facility Maintenance Division Annual Report

Recommended Motion:  Motion to receive and file.

Report Summary: The following is a report on what this Division has performed and
accomplished during the past year.

This year the Park Facilities division hosted, set up, and tore down a variety of
Centennial events throughout the year along with annual City events such as the Winter
Wonder Land, Azalea Festival, reservations, sports events, food giveaways, classes,
culminating with the Centennial Time Capsule Event.

We purchased disinfecting equipment, such as electronic handheld disinfectant
sprayers, floor auto-scrubbing machines and portable pressure washing machines.
These purchases expanded and improved our abilities to properly disinfect all Parks
facilities.

During the hurricane in August of 2023, we opened the Auditorium up as an emergency
shelter. Also, staff worked around the clock removing debris/trees from streets, handing
out sandbags to residents, and worked overlapping shifts for 24-hour coverage.

We added a weekend Park Facility Maintenance Lead Worker position during this time.
This position will ensure continuous supervision during the entire week as well as the
weekend.

The Community Service Worker Program is currently accepting up to fifteen volunteers
for facilities and more when needed to assist Facility Maintenance and Grounds staff.

Staff schedules have been changed to accommodate the expansion of classes and
reservations.

Facility staff has done a fine job transitioning from regular activities to new demands at
a moment’s notice.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 4
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Glenn Massey, Parks Superintendent
Date:  January 22, 2024
Subject:  Grounds & Parks Facility Maintenance - 2nd Quarter Review FY
  2023/24

Recommended Motion: Motion to Receive and File

Grounds Maintenance
During this quarter we hosted the Halloween event, Winter Wonderland at City Hall, and
the Christmas Parade. At the end of the parade on lot number three we set up the Show
Mobile for Santas Village. Everything went according to plan, staff picked up trash
during the event and there was no major impact to the Boy’s Scout Area.

We continue to host monthly food giveaways for the community at two locations, one at
Circle Park and the other at Hollydale Regional Park.

Tree trimming was completed at South Gate Park and the landscape project adjacent to
the Tot Lot at Hollydale Park was also completed. Baseball diamond number 9 and 2
were renovated during this quarter

Staff continue servicing and beautifying over 190 acres of park land on a daily basis.

Park Facility Maintenance
Parks Facility Maintenance along with Grounds staff set up and hosted Halloween
event, Rotary Club Thanksgiving Dinner, Winter Wonderland at City Hall, Breakfast with
Santa, Christmas Parade, and Pageant of Trees.

During this quarter we promoted Francisco Muñoz from Park Facility Maintenance
Worker to Park Facility Maintenance Lead Worker. He is assigned Thursday to Sunday,
to cover weekend events.

Due to the high use of SG Park, Staff continues to do a third daily inspection and
cleaning, in the late afternoon to our outdoor restrooms.

We have continued the use of Electrostatic Disinfecting Equipment for more coverage in

  Page 1 of 2
  46
 our cleaning and disinfecting efforts for both indoor and outdoor restroom facilities,
along with a pressure washing program. These disinfecting and cleaning tools will be
used consistently. Set ups for all events require us to disinfect all tables, chairs, door
handles, and A/V equipment.

We are in full operation with classes, as well as private rentals, picnics, sports activities,
and service clubs’ events. We continue to host monthly food giveaways for the
community at two locations, one at Circle Park and one at Hollydale Regional Park.

The Community Service Worker program is ongoing; we are still limiting intake to 15
people maximum per day.

Parks are busy with many events, classes, picnics, and sports activities. Although
pandemic mandates have been lifted, we remain vigilant when addressing the ongoing
challenges with restroom cleanliness with a routine restroom disinfecting program. This
includes the use of the C3 Machine to apply disinfectants and cleaners. Once product is
sprayed, staff scrubs floors, walls, and fixtures to insure sanitary conditions.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 5
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Rec.
Date:  January 22, 2024
Subject:  Recreation Programing Report – 2nd Quarter Review FY 2023/24

Recommended Motion: Motion to Receive and File

Aquatics
The second quarter continued with our most popular swim programs and closed with
exciting new Special Events that are here to stay. Despite the reduction in hours of
operation due to daylight savings and colder climate, October-December still witnessed
a continued commitment by the community to frequent the Patricia G. Mitchell Swim
Stadium.

Our Learn-To-Swim program instructed over 950 patrons in group, private, and semi-
private classes. Approximately 605 of them were youth ages 6-17 and 230 were Tiny
Tots ages 3-5. Pre-Competitive Swim Class and Junior Water Polo continued their
success during the second quarter by having close to 70 registrants. Additionally, staff
conducted a First Aid/CPR class for 15 community members and 10 staff.

October was an exciting month as the Swim Stadium hosted its first-ever floating
pumpkin patch, Patti’s Pumpkin Plunge. There were two sessions available, with each
session selling out within the first few weeks of advertising. Registrants had the
opportunity to pick their pumpkin in the shallow end and then decorate it on the patio
using the creative art stations that staff constructed. All in attendance received a goodie
bag and several prizes were raffled off.

In December, the Patricia G. Mitchell Swim Stadium hosted its inaugural Surfing with
Santa. Over 100 people registered for the event. Activities included arts and crafts,
snowball fights, surfing in the deep end with Santa’s elves, musical chairs, donut racing
in the water, and pictures with Santa & Mrs. Claus. Staff received great reviews and the
community really enjoyed themselves as was evident with the smiles on everyone’s
faces.

  Page 1 of 5
  48
 Fitness
Whether it’s the holidays, or the colder weather, our second quarter has traditionally
been one of our slowest periods, but this year was different. Our membership base
finished strong with just over 4,000 sold/renewed memberships. Once again, our
Fitness tier is the most popular, with the Adult category leading the way as usual. We
also saw a fifteen percent membership increase in the Senior category, which could be
attributed to the increase in Yoga and senior Group Exercise classes offered.
Daily Admissions stayed consistent with very similar numbers to our first quarter. We
had 2,979 daily admissions; 1,425 of them coming from adults who play basketball. Our
next closest category was teens who paid for basketball court use, which accounted for
416 daily admissions.
Our Personal Training program saw an increase, with 285 hours of training conducted.
The Private, 12-session option continues to be our most popular option. Our second
most popular was the Semi-private 16-session option, where members bring a partner
and participate in a session together. Semi-private sessions have seen a decrease
over the past few years, which may have been a result of covid and people wanting to
distance themselves.

Youth Sports
The first quarter began with all youth Fundamental sport classes filled to capacity or
near capacity. Our core group (basketball, volleyball, baseball, multi-sport, and soccer)
fundamental classes continue to be popular and provide introductory drills and lessons
to the aforementioned sports. Also, the Youth Sports Division held a Soccer Clinic with
18 registrants. All participants received technique instruction, individual/team drills, and
scrimmage play. At the conclusion of the clinic, everyone was awarded a certificate of
completion with a sack pack full of soccer swag. Contract classes (Tennis and Karate)
remained consistent and near capacity.

Adult Sports:
Our second quarter of Adult Sports ended with multiple divisions unable to conclude
due to rain. Currently, two Men’s Divisions require playoffs; games have been
postponed multiple weeks in a row. This season brought in 36 total teams across 6
divisions who battled weekly for the top spot. Champions were awarded the newly re-
designed Championship hoodies while 2nd place winners received customized insulated
South Gate water bottles.
Open play volleyball continues to thrive on Tuesday evenings and brought in 481 drop-
in participants this quarter.
Our popular BAD (Ballin After Dark) event took place the day before Thanksgiving and
was a rousing success. Twelve teams battle through pool play and then a single
elimination tournament to be the night’s King of the Court. A new champion was
crowned, and each team member received an Under Armor basketball bag and plenty
of ice to aid with the guaranteed 5 games. We are currently in the recruiting stage for
the next Men’s and Women’s basketball leagues.

Partner Organizations:
SG Aztecs have begun off season practices for Football and Cheer.
SGJAA began their Winter Basketball league with games on Mondays, Wednesdays,

  Page 2 of 5
  49
 Thursdays, and Saturdays. They are accepting registration for their Spring baseball
and softball seasons.
AYSO has concluded their Fall season and are currently taking registrations for the
spring season.

Social Media:
Our total followers are now up to 4,785. Last quarter we had 9 posts, and 148 stories.
We have reached over 10,000 accounts and engaged with 789. We have hired a
Recreation Marketing Coordinator to oversee the Social Media Task Force and all social
media outlets.

Senior Center:
Our fall season was very active this year as we scheduled and visited multiple sites for
our community excursions. October kicked off our fall excursions with 7 scheduled trips
(Fantasy Springs Casino, The Cheech Museum, Dia de los Muertos at Hollywood
Forever Cemetery, Morongo Casino, Aquarium of the Pacific, Elf the Musical, and Viejas
Casino). Each excursion was a success with all trips being filled at capacity or near
maximum capacity. Many of our seniors expressed an interest in having a scheduled
Loteria time, staff was able to accommodate the request and we now offer drop in
Loteria play on Tuesday’s. Yoga was another request that recently came in from our
seniors, staff was able to secure a new group exercise instructor and yoga is now being
offered on Monday’s & Thursday’s at 9:00am. Keeping in line with our goals for the year
of offering monthly socials for our seniors, this quarter started with a Halloween party.
This event brought a lot of smiles to many faces, our seniors also had the opportunity to
dress up and act like kids again. Our event consisted of the following: trick or treating,
raffles. and a costume contest. Our team also hosted a special Thanksgiving lunch for
the seniors with light refreshments and pastries, our Blue Jays dance group performed
and provided great entertainment. We wrapped up this quarter with our Christmas
social; our seniors enjoyed goodie bags, eggnog, and raffles. The celebration did not
stop there, the party really began when the dance floor opened, and the karaoke began.
December is a short month, and our facilities close for the holiday break, but HSA
continued to offer our lunch program for any seniors who attended.

Contract/ Youth Classes:
Fall contract classes operated as normal with the same classes being offered. Classes
worked hard for 8 weeks to learn and perform their routines at our dance recitals. To
accommodate all classes, we hosted two recitals: one on Monday, November 20 and
the other on Tuesday, November 21. Recitals were held at the Henry C. Gonzalez
Auditorium from 5:30pm-7:30pm, all dancers were given two tickets and had the
opportunity to purchase additional tickets if needed. Each night brought in 500
spectators per show and the children’s faces were priceless. In addition to the recitals
our Hip Hop and Mexican Folk classes also performed during the Winter Wonderland
event. Our internal programming for youth stayed consistent as all classes were near
maximum capacity. Our Tot-Time and Tiny Two classes hosted multiple themed

  Page 3 of 5
  50
 celebrations in their classrooms with their culminating pajama party/movie day for the
last day of classes. Lil Chefs created Halloween inspired recipes with all participants
enjoying their delicious treats.

Special Events:
Just like many divisions within our department, Fall was busy. Starting off strong, our
Parks and Recreation team held their Annual Halloween Haunt. The event took place on
October 31 from 6-9PM in the large quad in South Gate Park. The event had over 35
games booths that patrons could play and receive toys and/or candy.  Photo
opportunities were spread throughout the event so patrons could take photos with their
friends and family. DJ Gilbert was playing the hottest tunes and had the crowd pumped
up; we held our costume contests and numerous dance competitions for patrons to
receive goodie bag prizes. The Halloween Haunt also brought back our children’s
jumper area with a total of three jumpers for kids to play in. Lastly, the event had our
trackless trains offering rides to over the 5,000 people in attendance.

For the month of November, our department held the Annual Veterans Day event on
November 11, from 11am to 1pm at South Gate Park. There was a total of 75 people in
attendance, with light refreshments distributed. Every veteran in attendance was gifted
a remembrance medal and hat. The Legacy Cadet Corp from Legacy High School and
the K-Kids from Willow Elementary assisted with the Call to Honor, leading the pledge of
allegiance, and reading letters to veterans. Wrapping up the month of December, our
department helped put together the first ever Winter Wonderland event on Tuesday,
December 5, from 4pm to 8pm at South Gate City Hall. Over 900 wristbands were
passed out to children to participate in the night’s activities (Snowball fight, snow play,
snow globe photo op., and the sled run) and to receive a gift from Santa. Churros and
hot chocolate were distributed to all patrons. In addition to Winter Wonderland, we held
our annual Santa’s Breakfast event on December 9, from 9am to 1pm at the Auditorium.
This event sold out and had a total of 300 participants. Those in attendance were
served breakfast consisting of sausage, pancakes, milk, and orange juice. Children
attending the event participated in two craft areas and were able to write letters to Santa
and place them in Santa’s mailbox. Lastly, each child was gifted their own gingerbread
house kit and was able to take pictures with Santa and the Grinch. Raffles ended the
event with the chance to win gift cards, two bikes, and three Christmas trees.

Cultural Arts:
Our 3rd Annual South Gate Art Walk was hosted on October 14, the art walk was
composed of over 56 vendors/artisans/artists displaying/vending their work. In
collaboration with five partner organizations leading art workshops, we also had two DJs
(one on the main stage and one in front of the courthouse), three bands (performances
on the show mobile), and three live artists drawing/painting. We had over 500
community members in attendance and enjoyed an afternoon full of art and culture. It
was also the closing day for our Process/Proceso exhibit which we were able to

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 6
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Steve Costley, Director of Parks & Recreation
Date:  March 27, 2024
Subject:  Proposed Program Fees for 2024/25

Recommended Motion:  Approve the Proposed Program Fee Schedule for May 12,
2024, to May 11, 2025.

Report Summary: On a regular basis, the Parks & Recreation Department reviews the
fees they charge for different programs offered by the Department so that they can be
brought in-line with the costs to provide the programs. Annually, we bring to the
Commission a report on the fees and any proposed changes that are being
recommended for the upcoming fiscal year.

Last year the Parks & Recreation Department raised rates for programs/classes by 7%
in large part due to the inflation pressure from the past year. The only exception to the
price increase was the Tot Time program which had seen significant drops in
registration in the previous years and staff felt it would be best to leave pricing the same
to encourage additional signups in this program.

As the Commission is aware, inflation has slowed a little (3.4% higher than last year),
and the Minimum Wage in California was increased from $15.50 hr. to $16.00 hr. in
January of this year. Thus, staff is recommending that certain fees be increased for this
year while other fees remain the same. Staff feels that basic program fees are still low
as compared to other cities and moving them up to cover inflation will not dramatically
hurt the registration for those activities. On the other hand, fees in the Adult Sports
category have consistently moved up in the City over the past several years and now
we are finding that teams are moving to other leagues due to cost considerations and
any move to increase those fees will just lessen the number of teams that sign up.

In addition, the fees for Sports Center memberships were just reimagined a year ago
and it is recommended that they stay the same for the second year so that we can keep
increasing the attendance back up to pre-Covid numbers.

Attached is the Fee Schedule showing current fees and the proposed new fees. Staff
will be on hand to answer questions.
